Purchase to receipt

Buy raw materials on a purchase order and receive them into a warehouse.

Status
Walked 4 of 6
Module
Procurement, Warehousing
Length
6 tasks, 32 steps
Updated
22 Oct 2026
Applies to
Infor LN

Before you start

  • Know the item's stock before you start: Check an item's inventory.
  • The materials exist as items with purchase defaults, and the receiving warehouse exists. Configure the purchased group and Create the three items build both. A buy-from business partner must also exist — Purchase to receipt selects one and does not create one.

Procedure

1Read the baseline

Result
On-hand at the receiving warehouse is recorded before anything is booked.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000

Why LN works this way. Nothing yet. A confirmed receipt is a document reaching a status; only the on-hand figure at the receiving warehouse proves stock moved, and it cannot prove anything unless it was read before the order existed. A new item is not necessarily at zero.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000 and identify the raw-material warehouse you are buying intoWrite downreceiving warehousethe walked run used the raw-materials warehouse
1.2Filter for the first material and read its on-hand at that warehouseWrite downmaterial 1 code andmaterial 1 on-hand before
1.3Repeat for the second materialWrite downmaterial 2 code andmaterial 2 on-hand before
1.4Record both figures before booking anythingBoth baselines are written down, not remembered

2Create the purchase order

Result
An order exists against a buy-from business partner.
Screen
Procurement➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench tdpur4601m200

Why LN works this way. The buy-from business partner decides most of the header: LN defaults the Purchase Order Type, Purchase Office and Buyer from the partner record, falling back to the user profile where the partner leaves a field empty. The workbench opens the Purchase Order session to carry the order; the lookup only selects a partner and never creates one.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Purchase Order Intake Workbench tdpur4601m200The intake workbench opens
2.2Start a new orderA blank Purchase Order tdpur4100m900 opens
2.3Open the lookup on Buy-from Business Partner. It is Buy-from Business Partners tccom4520m000
2.4Select the partnerWrite downbuy-from business partnerthe walked run used one of the standard test partners
2.5Confirm the Purchase Order Type LN defaulted from the partnerThe walked run showed IPO (Inventory Purchase Order)
2.6Confirm the Purchase Office LN defaulted from the partnerThe partner's purchase office
2.7Save the headerWrite downpurchase order number andorder type

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Order type is not IPONothing. IPO is what the walked run defaulted, not a required value

3Book the lines

Result
Each material is ordered in the right quantity, to the right warehouse.

Why LN works this way. Each line names an item, a quantity and a warehouse, and the warehouse on the line is what LN will raise the inbound order against in Receive against the order. A line saved to the wrong warehouse produces a receipt that never reaches the stock you meant to build.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open the order's linesThe line grid is empty
3.2Add a line for the first material, with the quantity your downstream demand requiresWrite downmaterial 1 quantity orderedthe walked run booked line 10, BAM-ROD, 2.0000 ea
3.3Add a line for the second materialWrite downmaterial 2 quantity orderedthe walked run booked line 20, BAM-SLEEVE, 1.0000 ea
3.4Set the warehouse on every line to the receiving warehouse from step 1.1Both lines point at the receiving warehouse in the walked run — this is what decides where the goods land
3.5Save the linesBoth lines are stored against the order from step 2.7

4Receive against the order

Result
LN's generated inbound order is found and receiving is started.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders whinh2100m000

Why LN works this way. You do not create this order; the purchase order generates a warehousing order whose origin, purchase, gives it inbound activities. That is the handoff from Procurement to Warehousing. The purchase order's own Release to Warehousing tab shows which lines are still waiting, and its line status session says which activity has to happen first.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Open Warehousing Orders whinh2100m000
4.2Find the order LN generated from the purchase order
4.3Click Drill InAn inbound order exists that you did not create by hand
4.4Confirm its Order Type and ship-fromWrite downwarehousing order numberthe walked run showed order type PUI "Purchase Receipts", ship-from the partner from step 2.4, ship-to the receiving warehouse from step 1.1
4.5Select the inbound linesThe lines correspond to the purchase order lines from Book the lines
4.6Run Actions➔Receive on the selected inbound linesWarehouse Receipt whinh3512m000 opens

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
No warehousing order appears after saving the purchase orderThe warehouse on the order lines (step 3.4). Without one, there is nothing for LN to raise an inbound order against. Then the purchase order's Release to Warehousing tab: a line still sitting there has not been released, and Purchase Order Line Status tdpur4534m000 names the activity it is waiting on
The Actions menu offers no receive commandThe order origin. An outbound order carries outbound activities; confirm you opened the generated inbound order from step 4.1, not the purchase order

5Confirm the receipt

Result
The receipt reaches Confirmed with all lines final and complete.

Why LN works this way. The receive command lands you in a receipt whose lines LN built from the inbound order lines you linked, and confirming it is what books the goods. Every flag on the header summarises its lines, so Confirmed is cleared both when a line is unconfirmed and when there are no lines at all.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Read the receipt number LN assignedWrite downreceipt number
5.2Enter the packing-slip reference for each line as deliveredThe walked run recorded packing slips 123 (rod) and 124 (sleeve)
5.3Confirm the receiptStatus = Confirmed, and the header's Confirmed check box is set once every receipt line is confirmed
5.4Check All Lines Final and All Lines CompleteBoth are set — a receipt confirmed with either clear has left something behind
5.5Read Errors Logged before leaving the sessionClear means the receipt logged nothing. Set means it did, whatever the status says
5.6If Errors Logged is set, read the messages in Receipt Message Log whinh3530m000. They are also on the Message Log tab in this session's lines pane
5.7Then capture themThe messages behind the confirmation are on record.

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
whinh0032 at the receiptThe message names missing stock point details for the receipt line. Capture the LOG detail before clearing it — and afterwards, read the receipt's Errors Logged flag and Receipt Message Log whinh3530m000, which hold the messages once the dialog is gone
The receipt looks confirmed but nothing was receivedWhether the receipt has any lines at all. whinh3512m000's help states Confirmed is cleared when the receipt has no receipt lines — the same cleared box as a receipt whose lines are merely unconfirmed

6Verify the inventory increase

Result
On-hand rose by exactly the quantity received.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000

Why LN works this way. Nothing new. This task re-reads the figure from Read the baseline, because the receipt reaching Confirmed is not the proof; the number changing by exactly the received quantity is. A difference that is not the ordered quantity means something else moved stock in between, and adjusting it to match buries the evidence.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Re-read the first material at the receiving warehouseWrite downmaterial 1 on-hand afterup by exactly the quantity from step 3.2
6.2Re-read the second materialWrite downmaterial 2 on-hand afterup by exactly the quantity from step 3.3
6.3Compare both against the baselines from steps 1.2 and 1.3Each difference equals what was ordered and received, with nothing unexplained

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
The receipt confirms but on-hand does not moveWhether All Lines Final and All Lines Complete were both set (step 5.4), and whether the receiving warehouse in this task is the one from step 1.1

Variations

CaseWhat changesTask
Purchase with inspectionAn inspection activity sits between receipt and put-away. Warehouse Inspections whinh3122m000 runs against the receipt. This adds a task and would earn its own process.
Direct-delivery purchaseGoods ship from the supplier to a customer without entering your warehouse. That removes receiving, confirming and the inventory check entirely, so it is a different process, not a variant of this one
Booking opening stock instead of buyingThe adjustment route the notes of Stock the components describe — a cycle counting/adjustment order. Faster, but it bypasses purchase defaults and leaves no purchase price history. Its entry session was never captured
